Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then apply the required wake-visual inspection skill before changing any policy. After that I’ll trace the assigned parent, sampled results, inherited logs, and current rollout evidence into one candidate plus the two required documentation updates.

The contract confirms the candidate file must stay continuously non-empty, notes must precede the policy edit, and the final checker—not a local CFD run—is the required verification. I’m now using the wake-visual-signals skill because this task specifically requires diagnosing a multi-wake rollout before altering the target controller.

The sampled result is a finite but severe domain-exit failure: it briefly gets within 8.61 L, then travels mostly downward (−13.30 L in y versus −3.55 L in x), with both acceleration channels reaching their 1800°/time² limits. The compact JSON supplies the missing wake diagnostics inside the workspace, so I can cross-check the visual sheet without following its external artifact paths.

The release sheet makes the failure mode unambiguous: the seed rapidly pitches nearly vertical, follows a tight high-frequency oscillatory descent along the right side, never enters the target’s developed-wake neighborhood, and exits through the lower boundary. That agrees with the tiny net target progress, large lateral displacement/load, and actuator saturation; the useful inherited mechanism is propulsion, while the missing capability is bounded target-relative heading control.

I’m keeping the one-candidate change deliberately narrow: retain the seed’s autonomous traveling-bend oscillator, but center it on a smooth body-frame bearing correction and slow it enough that its nominal joint accelerations no longer demand the hard cap. The hypothesis is falsifiable in the next rollout by trajectory topology (x progress versus y drift), target distance, domain-exit class, and saturation/effort—not by score alone.

The skill-driven diagnosis and candidate hypothesis are now recorded in [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md), satisfying the required pre-edit provenance step. I’m applying that single policy candidate now.

The candidate and durable experience bank are both updated. The reusable lesson records the concrete negative boundary—target-blind propulsion plus capped demands produced self-motion but no directional control—and explicitly leaves the proposed bearing remedy unproven until the later CFD evaluation. I’m now invoking the three non-CFD checks specified by the workspace’s check-runner.

The first check exposed a pre-existing rendered-contract defect: `README.md` marks the same parent guidance example as “copied to guidance/” twice, while the checker requires exactly one marker. I’m inspecting the checker’s selection logic before making the smallest in-workspace repair, then I’ll rerun it.

The duplicate parent marker was the sole cause of the first failure; I removed only the redundant identical entry, and the guidance/notes check now passes. Next are the parameter-schema/policy execution check and the editable-boundary check.

The policy contract command is blocked by the runtime image, not by an assertion: `julia` is absent from the command path (the shell also emitted unrelated missing-SSH setup warnings before reaching it). I’ll check the workspace/runtime for an available Julia executable without running CFD; if none exists, I’ll still run the deterministic schema guard and boundary validator that do not require Julia.

The boundary check passes, confirming that exactly one solver file differs and it is the permitted candidate. No Julia executable exists anywhere in this workspace or the runtime’s standard locations, so the Julia execution check cannot run here; the deterministic schema guard passes with every `params.FIELD` declared and no candidate-owned `L`. I’m also invoking the configured check-runner as requested for an independent read-only verification of the same non-CFD checks.
